Question: If \[ \begin{gathered} \log_2(\log_3(\log_4x))=0,\\ \log_3(\log_4(\log_2y))=0,\\ \log_4(\log_2(\log_3z))=0, \end{gathered} \] then \(x+y+z\) is equal to:
Solution:
For a valid base \(b>0\), \(b\ne1\), the statement \(\log_b T=c\) means \(T=b^c\), with \(T>0\). In particular, a logarithm equals zero exactly when its argument is \(b^0=1\). All the bases here are valid.

Starting with the outermost logarithm in the first equation gives
\[
\begin{aligned}
\log_3(\log_4x)&=1,\\
\log_4x&=3,\\
x&=4^3=64.
\end{aligned}
\]
Applying the same definition to the second equation gives
\[
\begin{aligned}
\log_4(\log_2y)&=1,\\
\log_2y&=4,\\
y&=2^4=16.
\end{aligned}
\]
For the third equation,
\[
\begin{aligned}
\log_2(\log_3z)&=1,\\
\log_3z&=2,\\
z&=3^2=9.
\end{aligned}
\]
The arguments encountered in these three nested expressions are respectively \(64,3,1\), \(16,4,1\), and \(9,2,1\). They are all positive, so every logarithm is defined. Each reversal was an equivalence, so these values are uniquely determined.

Therefore \(x+y+z=64+16+9=89\), choice C.
